analytes: Lead, cadmium, arsenic, mercury, BPA, BPS, pesticides
key_findings: 47% exceeded at least one federal or state safety level; 21% exceeded 2x the California Prop 65 lead level; 28% of whey powders exceeded Prop 65 for lead vs 77% of plant and 79% of organic products
reported_limitation: Cohort-level percentages, not per-product concentrations; advocacy organisation; products purchased at retail

study: Clean Label Project Protein Study 2.0 - flavor effect
key_findings: Chocolate-flavored powders had about 4x the lead of vanilla; cocoa has been reported to carry up to 110x more cadmium than vanilla formulations
reported_limitation: Cocoa is the likely driver; magnitude varies by cocoa source and lot

study: Clean Label Project Protein Study 2.0 - plant vs whey
key_findings: Plant powders averaged about 3x the lead and 5x the cadmium of whey; collagen 26% exceeded Prop 65 for lead
reported_limitation: Aggregate comparison; whey is not contaminant-free

key_findings: 16 products were non-detect for all four metals, including 12 whey/dairy products such as ON Gold Standard Vanilla Ice Cream, Dymatize ISO100 Gourmet Vanilla, Isopure Unflavored, Premier Protein 100% Whey Vanilla, Garden of Life Grass Fed Whey Vanilla and Body Fortress Vanilla
reported_limitation: Non-detect is method-dependent; vanilla and unflavored products dominate the list

key_findings: More than two-thirds exceeded CR's 0.5 ug/day lead level in one serving; about 70% exceeded 120% of that level; plant-based averaged 9x the lead of dairy-based; highest were Naked Nutrition Vegan Mass Gainer (7.7 ug) and Huel Black Edition (6.3 ug)
threshold_used: CR level of concern 0.5 ug/day lead; 4.1 ug cadmium; 7 ug arsenic
reported_limitation: 23 products; not a statistical sample; CR assumes one serving per day

key_findings: Clean Simple Eats whey 0.21 ug/serving, Equate whey 0.27, Premier Protein 0.38, Truvani plant 0.46, Ritual plant 0.53; four of five below CR's level of concern
reported_limitation: Small confirmatory sample; shows low-lead products are manufacturable

analytes: Trace elements by ICP-MS and LIBS
key_findings: No sample exceeded regulatory limits for lead, cadmium, arsenic or mercury
reported_limitation: Small market sample; methods sensitive but limits are permissive

study: Human health risk assessment of CR data
key_findings: Estimated chronic daily intake from 1-3 servings: arsenic 0.2-16.9 ug/day, cadmium 0-5.6, mercury 0-1.1, lead 0-13.5; weight gainers had significantly higher arsenic
reported_limitation: Risk assessment of someone else's measurements; exposure assumptions drive conclusions

study: FDA enforcement - no lead limit for supplements
key_findings: FDA has no enforceable lead limit specific to protein powders or dietary supplements; CR petitioned FDA to set one in October 2025
threshold_used: Prop 65 used as de facto benchmark
reported_limitation: Regulatory gap, not a measured finding
